name: Search – WordWheelQuery
purpose: Maintains an ordered history of the search terms a user has typed into the File Explorer search box.
key_fields: Numbered values - each holding one Unicode search term string
MRUListEx - binary DWORD-array giving the order terms were entered, most recent first
Key LastWrite time - approximates when the most recent search term was entered
normal_baseline: A handful of everyday search terms (partial filenames, project names, common file extensions) consistent with the user routinely locating their own files.
anomalies: Search terms for file extensions or keywords associated with sensitive data categories (passwords, finance, HR, credentials, wallet, config) shortly before a data-access or exfiltration incident
Search terms naming security tools, log files, or forensic artifacts (event log names, AV product names) suggesting reconnaissance or anti-forensic intent
Search terms for another user's name or profile-specific paths, suggesting lateral browsing of another account's data
A burst of many distinct search queries in a very short window, inconsistent with normal manual typing
anti_forensic_notes: WordWheelQuery is not touched by mainstream browser-focused privacy cleaners, so its survival alongside cleared browser history can point an analyst toward local file-system searching that other tools missed. The key can still be cleared directly via registry edit, and its complete absence on an otherwise active profile is itself worth noting.
interpretation: Search terms are stored in Unicode and ordered purely by the MRUListEx sequence, not by embedded timestamps within each value - only the key's overall LastWrite time anchors the list in time, so establishing when an earlier (non-most-recent) search term was entered is not possible from this artifact alone.
